records.source: Περὶ δὲ τῶν πνευματικῶν, ἀδελφοί, οὐ θέλω ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν.
records.gloss: Concerning now the spiritual [things], brothers, not I want you to be ignorant.
pieces: Now about spiritual gifts, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}: I want you to be well informed.

L.1: Now concerning the spiritual [gifts], {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, I do not want you to be ignorant.

R.1: Now, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, I want to teach you about the gifts that the Spirit gives. I want you to understand them clearly.

decisions.choice: now concerning: Paul takes up a new subject, probably one the Corinthians raised in their letter
decisions.reason: Περὶ δὲ opens a new topic, as at 7:1, 7:25 and 8:1. Chapters 12-14 all deal with this subject: what the Spirit gives and how it is used when the church meets.

decisions.choice: the spiritual things: the gifts that come from the Spirit
alternatives: spiritual people, those who have the Spirit's gifts
decisions.reason: τῶν πνευματικῶν can be neuter, "the spiritual things", or masculine, "the spiritual people". The neuter fits 14:1, where the same word clearly means gifts, and the subject of 12:4-11. The masculine fits 14:37 ("if anyone thinks he is a prophet or spiritual"), and some in Corinth may have claimed to be the spiritual ones (3:1). Either way the chapter is about the Spirit's gifts and those who use them.

decisions.choice: I do not want you to be ignorant: a formula Paul uses to introduce something important
decisions.reason: The same phrase opens new teaching in 10:1, Romans 1:13 and 1 Thessalonians 4:13. It is not a rebuke; it calls attention to what follows.

decisions.choice: the spiritual [gifts] (L); spiritual gifts (B); the gifts that the Spirit gives (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek has only the adjective; the levels supply "gifts" as chosen in m2, and the footnote gives "spiritual people".

decisions.choice: I want you to be well informed (B); I want you to understand them clearly (R)
alternatives: I do not want you to be ignorant
I do not want you to be uninformed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say positively what the double negative means (m3); "ignorant" now sounds like an insult.

records.heading: Gifts from the one Spirit

records.source: οἴδατε ὅτι ὅτε ἔθνη ἦτε πρὸς τὰ εἴδωλα τὰ ἄφωνα ὡς ἂν ἤγεσθε ἀπαγόμενοι.
records.gloss: You know that when gentiles you were, to the idols the mute as ever you were led being led away.
pieces: You know how it was when you were pagans: you were swept off to idols that cannot speak, carried away whichever way you were led.

L.2: You know that when you were Gentiles, [you were] led away to the mute idols, however you were led.

R.2: You remember what your life was like before you believed. You were pulled this way and that, and you ended up worshiping idols that cannot even speak.

decisions.choice: gentiles: people outside God's people who worshiped other gods; pagans
alternatives: the nations, non-Jews as an ethnic group
decisions.reason: ἔθνη means the nations, people who are not Jews. Here Paul speaks of what the Corinthians were ("when you were"), as if they are no longer "gentiles": they still are not Jews, but they no longer live as people who do not know God (1 Thessalonians 4:5).

decisions.choice: however you were led: you were carried along again and again, by forces you did not control
alternatives: whenever you were led (on particular occasions such as festivals)
decisions.reason: ὡς ἂν with the imperfect ἤγεσθε describes something that happened repeatedly, and ἀπαγόμενοι ("being led away") is used for prisoners led off under guard. The sentence is broken in the Greek ("that when ... as you were led"), and Paul does not say who led them; 10:20 says that behind idols are demons.

decisions.choice: mute idols: idols that cannot speak
decisions.reason: The Scriptures mock idols that have mouths but cannot speak (Psalm 115:5; Habakkuk 2:18-19). The contrast prepares for verse 3: the Spirit of God does speak, through God's people.

decisions.choice: the Corinthians' former worship may have included ecstatic experiences
alternatives: the verse refers only to idol worship in general
decisions.reason: Some pagan cults in the Greek world, such as the worship of Dionysus, prized frenzied states in which a person felt seized by a god. If Paul has these in mind, his point is that being carried away is no proof of the Spirit; what is said about Jesus is (verse 3).

decisions.choice: pagans (B); before you believed (R)
decisions.reason: "Gentiles" would suggest only that they were not Jews; the point is that they worshiped idols (m1). Literal keeps "Gentiles".

records.source: διὸ γνωρίζω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδεὶς ἐν πνεύματι θεοῦ λαλῶν λέγει· Ἀνάθεμα Ἰησοῦς, καὶ οὐδεὶς δύναται εἰπεῖν· Κύριος Ἰησοῦς εἰ μὴ ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ.
records.gloss: Therefore I make known to you that no one by [the] Spirit of God speaking says, Accursed Jesus, and no one is able to say, Lord Jesus, except by [the] Spirit Holy.
pieces: That is why I am making this clear to you: nobody who speaks through God's Spirit ever says, "Jesus is cursed," and nobody can say, "Jesus is Lord," except through the Holy Spirit.

L.3: Therefore I make known to you that no one speaking by [the] Spirit of God says, "Jesus [is] accursed," and no one is able to say, "Jesus [is] Lord," except by [the] Holy Spirit.

R.3: So I want you to understand this. When the Spirit of God is leading people to speak, they never say, "Jesus is cursed." And only the Holy Spirit can lead someone to say, "Jesus is Lord."

decisions.choice: accursed: under God's curse, handed over to destruction
decisions.reason: Ἀνάθεμα is the word the Greek Old Testament uses for what is devoted to destruction (Deuteronomy 7:26). Paul uses it for one who is cut off and under God's curse (16:22; Romans 9:3; Galatians 1:8-9).

decisions.choice: who would cry "Jesus is accursed" is not known
alternatives: an outburst in ecstatic speech in the church
a demand made of believers in a synagogue or before a court
a statement Paul makes up to set beside the true confession
decisions.reason: Paul gives no setting. The cry may be invented to make the contrast sharp, or it may echo what Jesus' opponents said of one who was hanged on a tree (Galatians 3:13; Deuteronomy 21:23). His point is the same either way: speech that dishonors Jesus cannot come from God's Spirit, however inspired it sounds.

decisions.choice: Jesus is Lord: the basic confession of the Christian faith
decisions.reason: To say Κύριος Ἰησοῦς is to confess Jesus as the one with all authority (Romans 10:9; Philippians 2:11). The Greek Old Testament uses the same word for the God of Israel, so the confession puts Jesus where God alone belongs. No one makes it truly without the Spirit.

decisions.choice: by the Spirit: with the Spirit as the power at work in the speaker
alternatives: in the Spirit, in a state of inspiration
decisions.reason: ἐν πνεύματι can mean "by" or "in". The sense is that the Spirit moves the speaker; the test of whether the Spirit is at work is what is said about Jesus.

decisions.choice: Jesus [is] accursed / Jesus [is] Lord (L); Jesus is cursed / Jesus is Lord (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek has no verb in either saying. Both are read as statements; "Jesus be cursed" would make the first a wish, with much the same force.

records.source: Διαιρέσεις δὲ χαρισμάτων εἰσίν, τὸ δὲ αὐτὸ πνεῦμα·
records.gloss: Distributions now of gifts there are, but the same Spirit;
pieces: Gifts are given out in different ways, but it is the same Spirit who gives them.

L.4: Now there are distributions of gifts, but the same Spirit.

R.4: The Spirit gives different gifts to different people, but it is always the same Spirit.

decisions.choice: distributions: different gifts, given out to different people
decisions.reason: Διαιρέσεις can mean dividing out or allotting, and also the differences that result. The verb from the same root in verse 11 ("distributing to each") shows that the giving out is in view, and the list in verses 8-10 shows the variety.

decisions.choice: gifts: things given freely by God's grace
decisions.reason: χαρισμάτων is formed from the word for grace and means a gift of grace. In this chapter it names what the Spirit gives each believer for the good of all (verse 7). Paul uses the same word in 1:7 and 7:7, and it runs through chapters 12-14.

decisions.choice: the same Spirit: one giver behind every gift
decisions.reason: Verses 4-6 say the same thing three times: the gifts differ, the giver is one. The point answers a church divided over whose gift was best.

decisions.choice: gifts (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The word is rendered "gifts" at every level in chapters 12-14, so that readers can follow it; m2 notes its link with grace. 1:7 brings out that link in Balanced ("gift of grace"), where Paul has just spoken of grace.

decisions.choice: it is the same Spirit who gives them (B); it is always the same Spirit (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek has no verb in the second half; Balanced and Readable supply what the contrast implies.

records.source: καὶ διαιρέσεις διακονιῶν εἰσιν, καὶ ὁ αὐτὸς κύριος·
records.gloss: and distributions of ministries there are, and the same Lord;
pieces: Ministries are given out in different ways, and it is the same Lord who is served.

L.5: And there are distributions of ministries, and the same Lord.

R.5: There are different ways to serve, but we all serve the same Lord.

decisions.choice: ministries: ways of serving others
decisions.reason: διακονιῶν is service, work done for the good of others. Paul uses it for his own work as an apostle (2 Corinthians 4:1) and for practical help (16:15). The gifts are given to serve.

decisions.choice: the same Lord: Jesus Christ, whom all serve
decisions.reason: In this letter "Lord" alone usually means Jesus (8:6; 12:3). Whatever form the service takes, it is service to one Lord.

decisions.choice: it is the same Lord who is served (B); we all serve the same Lord (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek has no verb; Balanced and Readable say how the Lord is related to the ministries.

records.source: καὶ διαιρέσεις ἐνεργημάτων εἰσίν, ὁ δὲ αὐτὸς θεός, ὁ ἐνεργῶν τὰ πάντα ἐν πᾶσιν.
records.gloss: and distributions of workings there are, but the same God, the [one] working the all things in all.
pieces: Workings of power are given out in different ways, but it is the same God who works all of them in everyone.

L.6: And there are distributions of workings, but the same God, who works all things in all.

R.6: God's power works in different ways, but it is the same God who does all these things in every one of us.

decisions.choice: workings: what God's power produces, things done by his power at work
decisions.reason: ἐνεργημάτων is related to the verb ἐνεργῶν ("working") in the same verse. It names the results of God's power at work; verse 10 uses it for miracles.

decisions.choice: in all: in every believer
decisions.reason: πᾶσιν can be masculine or neuter. Verse 7, "to each", suggests people: God is at work in every member of the church.

decisions.choice: Spirit, Lord and God: one God at work in three persons
decisions.reason: Verses 4-6 name the Spirit, the Lord Jesus and God the Father side by side as the source of the gifts, as 2 Corinthians 13:13 does in a blessing. Paul is not teaching about the Trinity here, but his words assume it.

decisions.choice: workings of power
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out that these are the results of power at work (m1); Readable says "God's power works".

records.source: ἑκάστῳ δὲ δίδοται ἡ φανέρωσις τοῦ πνεύματος πρὸς τὸ συμφέρον.
records.gloss: To each now is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the benefiting.
pieces: Each person is given a way in which the Spirit is openly at work, and it is given for the good of all.

L.7: Now to each one is given the manifestation of the Spirit for [what is] beneficial.

R.7: In each one of us the Spirit is at work in a way that others can see. God gives this to help the whole church.

decisions.choice: the manifestation of the Spirit: the Spirit made visible, shown to be present and at work
decisions.reason: τοῦ πνεύματος can be the one who is shown or the one who shows. Since the list that follows describes gifts in which the Spirit's presence becomes evident, the Spirit is the one made known.

decisions.choice: for the benefit of all: given to do good to the church, not for the one who has it
alternatives: for what is profitable to the person
decisions.reason: τὸ συμφέρον means what is useful or brings benefit. In this letter the benefit is that of the church (10:23-24, 33; 14:3-5, 12).

decisions.choice: is given to each: God gives, and every believer receives
decisions.reason: δίδοται is passive, with God as the giver (verse 18; verse 28). ἑκάστῳ means each one: no believer is left out.

decisions.choice: a way in which the Spirit is openly at work (B); the Spirit is at work in a way that others can see (R)
decisions.reason: "Manifestation" is a hard word; Balanced and Readable say what it means (m1).

decisions.choice: God gives this to help the whole church
decisions.reason: Readable names the giver (m3) and says whose good is meant (m2).

records.source: ᾧ μὲν γὰρ διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος δίδοται λόγος σοφίας, ἄλλῳ δὲ λόγος γνώσεως κατὰ τὸ αὐτὸ πνεῦμα, ἑτέρῳ πίστις ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ πνεύματι, ἄλλῳ χαρίσματα ἰαμάτων ἐν τῷ ἑνὶ πνεύματι, ἄλλῳ ἐνεργήματα δυνάμεων, ἄλλῳ προφητεία, ἄλλῳ διακρίσεις πνευμάτων, ἑτέρῳ γένη γλωσσῶν, ἄλλῳ ἑρμηνεία γλωσσῶν·
records.gloss: To one for through the Spirit is given a word of wisdom, to another and a word of knowledge according to the same Spirit, \v 9 to another faith by the same Spirit, to another gifts of healings by the one Spirit, \v 10 to another workings of powers, to another prophecy, to another distinguishings of spirits, to another kinds of tongues, to another interpretation of tongues;
pieces: Through the Spirit one person is given a message of wisdom; another, by the same Spirit, a message of knowledge;
another, by the same Spirit, faith; another, by the one Spirit, gifts of healing;
another, the power to work miracles; another, prophecy; another, the ability to tell spirits apart; another, different kinds of tongues; and another, the interpretation of tongues.

L.8: For to one is given through the Spirit a word of wisdom, and to another a word of knowledge according to the same Spirit,
L.9: to another faith by the same Spirit, to another gifts of healings by the one Spirit,
L.10: to another workings of miracles, to another prophecy, to another distinguishing of spirits, to another kinds of tongues, to another interpretation of tongues.

R.8: The Spirit helps one person speak with wisdom. The same Spirit helps another person speak with knowledge.
R.9: The same Spirit gives one person a special gift of faith, and gives another person gifts to heal people.
R.10: One person has the power to do miracles. Another can prophesy. Another can tell which spirits are from God and which are not. One person can speak in different kinds of tongues, and another can interpret what is said in tongues.

decisions.choice: a word of wisdom, a word of knowledge: speech given by the Spirit that brings God's wisdom or knowledge to others
alternatives: wisdom and knowledge as qualities of mind
decisions.reason: λόγος shows these are gifts of speaking. Paul has contrasted human wisdom with the wisdom the Spirit reveals (2:6-13), and knowledge was prized in Corinth (8:1). He does not define how the two gifts differ.

decisions.choice: faith: a particular gift of faith, confidence that God will act in a given situation
alternatives: the faith that saves, which every believer has
decisions.reason: Every believer has saving faith, but this is given only to some. It is probably the faith that "moves mountains" (13:2; Mark 11:22-23).

decisions.choice: gifts of healings, workings of miracles: each healing and each miracle is itself a gift
decisions.reason: Both nouns are plural in each pair. δυνάμεων are acts of power, miracles (2 Corinthians 12:12; Galatians 3:5).

decisions.choice: prophecy: speaking a message from God for the church
decisions.reason: In chapter 14 prophecy builds up, encourages and comforts the church (14:3) and lays bare the secrets of the heart (14:24-25). It may include prediction (Acts 11:28) but is not limited to it.

decisions.choice: distinguishing of spirits: telling whether a spiritual utterance comes from God's Spirit or from another spirit
decisions.reason: The church was to test what was spoken under inspiration (14:29; 1 Thessalonians 5:20-21; 1 John 4:1). Verses 2-3 have just shown that not every inspired utterance comes from God.

decisions.choice: tongues: speech given by the Spirit in a language the speaker has not learned
alternatives: speech that is not any human language
decisions.reason: γλωσσῶν means both the tongue and a language. At Pentecost hearers recognized their own languages (Acts 2:4-11). In Corinth no one understood a tongue unless it was interpreted (14:2, 27-28), and Paul speaks of "tongues of angels" (13:1). "Kinds" of tongues may cover both.

decisions.choice: interpretation: putting into understandable words what was said in a tongue
alternatives: translation from one human language to another
decisions.reason: In chapter 14 interpretation lets the whole church understand and be built up by a tongue (14:5, 13, 27-28). It too is a gift of the Spirit.

decisions.choice: through, according to, by the one Spirit: every gift has the same source
decisions.reason: Paul varies the prepositions but says one thing: the Spirit gives them all (verse 11).

decisions.choice: names of the gifts: word of wisdom / knowledge (L), message of wisdom / knowledge (B); gifts of healing; workings of miracles (L), the power to work miracles (B); prophecy; distinguishing of spirits (L), the ability to tell spirits apart (B); kinds of tongues (L), different kinds of tongues (B); interpretation of tongues
decisions.reason: These names are kept wherever the gifts come back (12:28-30; chapters 13-14). "Message" makes clear that the first two are gifts of speaking (m1). "Tongues" keeps the one word Paul uses for the tongue and for speech; the footnote gives "languages" (m6).

decisions.choice: a special gift of faith; which spirits are from God and which are not
decisions.reason: Readable says that this faith is not the faith every believer has (m2), and what telling spirits apart means (m5).

records.source: πάντα δὲ ταῦτα ἐνεργεῖ τὸ ἓν καὶ τὸ αὐτὸ πνεῦμα, διαιροῦν ἰδίᾳ ἑκάστῳ καθὼς βούλεται.
records.gloss: All now these works the one and the same Spirit, distributing individually to each as he wills.
pieces: One and the same Spirit is at work in all of these, giving to each person separately as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chooses.

L.11: But all these [things] the one and the same Spirit works, distributing to each one individually as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wills.

R.11: It is the one Spirit who does all these things. The Spirit decides which gifts to give to each person.

decisions.choice: works: the Spirit does what verse 6 says God does
decisions.reason: ἐνεργεῖ repeats the verb of verse 6, where God "works all things in all". The Spirit is the one through whom God works.

decisions.choice: as he wills: the Spirit chooses, freely, which gift each person receives
alternatives: the gifts are given according to what each person wants or deserves
decisions.reason: βούλεται is a verb of willing and deciding, used of persons. The Spirit is not a force but acts with a will of his own. No one can boast about a gift, and no one should despise a gift as lesser (4:7).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}
decisions.reason: The Spirit is a person and is never "it"; the pronoun takes the deity_pronoun setting. Readable repeats "the Spirit".

records.source: Καθάπερ γὰρ τὸ σῶμα ἕν ἐστιν καὶ μέλη πολλὰ ἔχει, πάντα δὲ τὰ μέλη τοῦ σώματος πολλὰ ὄντα ἕν ἐστιν σῶμα, οὕτως καὶ ὁ Χριστός·
records.gloss: Just as for the body one is and members many has, all but the members of the body many being one are body, so also the Christ;
pieces: A body is a single whole, and yet it has many parts; all its parts, many as they are, make up one body. It is the same with {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

L.12: For just as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of the body, many as they are, are one body, so also [is] the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

R.12: A body is one thing, but it has many parts. It has many parts, but together they make one body. It is the same with {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people.

decisions.choice: members: the parts of a body, limbs and organs
decisions.reason: μέλη are the parts of a body, as in 6:15. The picture is physical throughout verses 12-26.

decisions.choice: so also is Christ: Christ is one with his people, who are his body
decisions.reason: Paul might have said "so also is the church"; he says "Christ". The church is Christ's own body (verse 27; 6:15; Ephesians 1:22-23), and in it Christ is present.

decisions.choice: the body as a picture of a community was familiar in the ancient world
decisions.reason: Greek and Roman writers used the body to urge citizens to keep their place for the good of the state; Livy tells such a fable of the Roman people (2.32). Paul uses the picture to say that every part matters and needs the others.

decisions.choice: parts (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 6:15: "members" now usually means members of a club, so Balanced and Readable keep the picture of a body (m1). Literal keeps "members".

decisions.choice: Christ and his people
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that Christ is meant together with those who belong to him (m2).

records.heading: One body with many parts

records.source: καὶ γὰρ ἐν ἑνὶ πνεύματι ἡμεῖς πάντες εἰς ἓν σῶμα ἐβαπτίσθημεν, εἴτε Ἰουδαῖοι εἴτε Ἕλληνες, εἴτε δοῦλοι εἴτε ἐλεύθεροι, καὶ πάντες ἓν πνεῦμα ἐποτίσθημεν.
records.gloss: Also for in one Spirit we all into one body were baptized, whether Jews or Greeks, whether slaves or free, and all one Spirit were made to drink.
pieces: Indeed, all of us were baptized in one Spirit into one body, whether we were Jews or Greeks, slaves or free, and all of us were given one Spirit to drink.

L.13: For indeed in one Spirit we all were baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, whether slaves or free, and all were given one Spirit to drink.

R.13: It does not matter whether we are Jews or Greeks, slaves or free. All of us were baptized in the one Spirit, and that made us one body. God gave every one of us the same Spirit, like water to drink.

decisions.choice: in one Spirit: the Spirit is the one in whom believers are baptized, as water is in baptism
alternatives: by one Spirit, the Spirit doing the baptizing
decisions.reason: ἐν can mean "in" or "by". John the Baptist said that the one coming would baptize "in the Holy Spirit" (Mark 1:8), with the Spirit as the element. "By" would make the Spirit the one who baptizes. Either way the Spirit unites believers into one body.

decisions.choice: baptized into one body: joined to Christ's body when they received the Spirit, the event that baptism marks
decisions.reason: "We all" were baptized: Paul speaks of what is true of every believer, not of some. Water baptism goes with it (Galatians 3:27-28; Romans 6:3), but the stress here is on the Spirit's work.

decisions.choice: Jews and Greeks, slaves and free: the deepest divisions of the ancient world, overcome in the one body
decisions.reason: "Greeks" means people who were not Jews. A slave was the legal property of another; the church in Corinth had both slaves and free people (7:21-22). Compare Galatians 3:28 and Colossians 3:11.

decisions.choice: made to drink: given the Spirit, as water is given to the thirsty or to dry ground
decisions.reason: ἐποτίσθημεν means to give drink or to water a field (3:6-8). The prophets promised that God would pour out his Spirit like water (Isaiah 32:15; 44:3), and Jesus spoke of the Spirit as living water (John 7:37-39). The two halves of the verse probably describe one event.

decisions.choice: were given one Spirit to drink (B); gave every one of us the same Spirit, like water to drink (R)
alternatives: were made to drink of one Spirit
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the picture of drinking and make it clear that the Spirit is given (m4).

decisions.choice: the list of Jews and Greeks, slaves and free comes first
decisions.reason: Readable starts with the differences, so that the point, one body, comes last.

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it in "slave or free" lists: the verse sets slave against free (m3).

records.source: Καὶ γὰρ τὸ σῶμα οὐκ ἔστιν ἓν μέλος ἀλλὰ πολλά.
records.gloss: Also for the body not is one member but many.
pieces: After all, a body does not consist of one part. It has many.

L.14: For indeed the body is not one member but many.

R.14: A body is not just one part. It has many parts.

decisions.choice: for indeed: Paul begins to explain the picture of verse 12
decisions.reason: Καὶ γὰρ introduces verses 15-26, which work out what it means for one body to have many parts.

decisions.choice: part (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 12, "part" keeps the picture of a body; Literal says "member".

records.source: ἐὰν εἴπῃ ὁ πούς· Ὅτι οὐκ εἰμὶ χείρ, οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐκ τοῦ σώματος, οὐ παρὰ τοῦτο οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ τοῦ σώματος;
records.gloss: If should say the foot, Because not I am hand, not I am of the body, not because of this not is it of the body?
pieces: Suppose the foot says, "I am not a hand, so I do not belong to the body." Would it belong to the body any less for that?

L.15: If the foot should say, "Because I am not a hand, I am not of the body," it is not for that reason not of the body, [is it]?

R.15: Suppose the foot said, "I am not a hand, so I am not part of the body." It would still be part of the body!

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer: it still belongs to the body
alternatives: a statement: it does not for that reason stop belonging to the body
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT punctuates this as a question; the two negatives together mean that saying so changes nothing. Read as a statement, the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: the foot speaks for believers who feel their gift makes them less a part of the church
decisions.reason: The foot compares itself with the hand and decides it does not belong. Verses 15-20 answer members who feel inferior; verses 21-26 answer those who look down on others.

decisions.choice: It would still be part of the body!
alternatives: Would it belong to the body any less?
decisions.reason: Readable gives the answer the question expects (m1).

records.source: καὶ ἐὰν εἴπῃ τὸ οὖς· Ὅτι οὐκ εἰμὶ ὀφθαλμός, οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐκ τοῦ σώματος, οὐ παρὰ τοῦτο οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ τοῦ σώματος·
records.gloss: And if should say the ear, Because not I am eye, not I am of the body, not because of this not is it of the body;
pieces: And if the ear says, "I am not an eye, so I do not belong to the body," it does not belong to the body any less for that.

L.16: And if the ear should say, "Because I am not an eye, I am not of the body," it is not for that reason not of the body.

R.16: Or suppose the ear said, "I am not an eye, so I am not part of the body." It would still be part of the body.

decisions.choice: it is not for that reason any less part of the body
decisions.reason: Verse 16 repeats verse 15, but the SBLGNT ends it with a raised dot rather than a question mark, so it reads as a statement. The meaning is the same: the ear still belongs.

decisions.choice: the ear and the eye: parts that seem to matter less and more
decisions.reason: The ear compares itself with the eye, the part people value most. As with the foot and the hand, the comparison does not change its place in the body.

records.source: εἰ ὅλον τὸ σῶμα ὀφθαλμός, ποῦ ἡ ἀκοή;
records.gloss: If whole the body [were] eye, where the hearing?
pieces: If the body were nothing but an eye, how would it hear?

L.17: If the whole body [were] an eye, where [would] the hearing [be]?

R.17: If the body were only an eye, it could not hear.

decisions.choice: hearing: the sense of hearing
decisions.reason: ἀκοή; is hearing, and so the ear that hears. Paul's point is that a body that was all eye would lack something it needs.

decisions.choice: it could not hear
decisions.reason: Readable gives the answer to the question instead of asking it.

records.source: εἰ ὅλον ἀκοή, ποῦ ἡ ὄσφρησις;
records.gloss: If whole [were] hearing, where the smelling?
pieces: If it were all ear, what would it smell with?

L.17: If the whole [were] hearing, where [would] the smelling [be]?

R.17: If it were only an ear, it could not smell.

decisions.choice: if the whole [body were] hearing
decisions.reason: ὅλον stands without "body", which carries over from the question before.

decisions.choice: ear
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the part, as the question about the eye does.

records.source: νυνὶ δὲ ὁ θεὸς ἔθετο τὰ μέλη, ἓν ἕκαστον αὐτῶν, ἐν τῷ σώματι καθὼς ἠθέλησεν.
records.gloss: But now the God placed the members, one each of them, in the body as he wanted.
pieces: But as things are, God has arranged each and every part in the body as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw fit.

L.18: But now God placed the members, each single one of them, in the body just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wished.

R.18: But God put each part of the body just where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wanted it.

decisions.choice: but now: but as it is, in reality
decisions.reason: νυνὶ here is logical, not about time: it turns from the absurd "if" of verses 17 to what is actually so.

decisions.choice: God placed each part as he chose
decisions.reason: God's will decides where each part goes, as the Spirit's will decides the gifts (verse 11). The same verb ἔθετο returns in verse 28: God placed people in the church.

records.source: εἰ δὲ ἦν τὰ πάντα ἓν μέλος, ποῦ τὸ σῶμα;
records.gloss: If but were the all one member, where the body?
pieces: If the whole were one single part, what kind of body would that be?

L.19: And if they were all one member, where [would] the body [be]?

R.19: If all the parts were the same, there would be no body.

decisions.choice: where would the body be?: there would be no body at all
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer that one part alone is not a body.

decisions.choice: there would be no body
decisions.reason: Readable gives the answer instead of the question.

records.source: νῦν δὲ πολλὰ μὲν μέλη, ἓν δὲ σῶμα.
records.gloss: Now but many on the one hand members, one but body.
pieces: As it is, the parts are many, but the body is one.

L.20: But now [there are] many members, but one body.

R.20: So there are many parts, but they make up only one body.

decisions.choice: but now: as things really are
decisions.reason: As in verse 18, νῦν turns from the impossible case to reality. The verse sums up verses 14-19.

records.source: οὐ δύναται δὲ ὁ ὀφθαλμὸς εἰπεῖν τῇ χειρί· Χρείαν σου οὐκ ἔχω, ἢ πάλιν ἡ κεφαλὴ τοῖς ποσίν· Χρείαν ὑμῶν οὐκ ἔχω·
records.gloss: Not is able but the eye to say to the hand, Need of you not I have, or again the head to the feet, Need of you not I have;
pieces: So the eye cannot tell the hand, "I can do without you," and the head cannot tell the feet, "I can do without you."

L.21: And the eye cannot say to the hand, "I have no need of you," or again the head to the feet, "I have no need of you."

R.21: An eye cannot tell a hand, "I can get along without you." A head cannot tell the feet, "I can get along without you."

decisions.choice: the parts that think themselves important cannot do without the others
decisions.reason: Verses 15-16 answered parts that felt they did not belong. Now Paul turns to parts that look down on others, as some in Corinth looked down on those without the gifts they prized.

decisions.choice: you, then you all: one hand, then both feet
decisions.reason: σου is singular and ὑμῶν plural, matching the hand and the feet.

decisions.choice: I can do without you (B); I can get along without you (R)
alternatives: I have no need of you
decisions.reason: The same words for both sayings, as in the Greek.

records.source: ἀλλὰ πολλῷ μᾶλλον τὰ δοκοῦντα μέλη τοῦ σώματος ἀσθενέστερα ὑπάρχειν ἀναγκαῖά ἐστιν, καὶ ἃ δοκοῦμεν ἀτιμότερα εἶναι τοῦ σώματος, τούτοις τιμὴν περισσοτέραν περιτίθεμεν, καὶ τὰ ἀσχήμονα ἡμῶν εὐσχημοσύνην περισσοτέραν ἔχει, τὰ δὲ εὐσχήμονα ἡμῶν οὐ χρείαν ἔχει.
records.gloss: But much rather the seeming members of the body weaker to be necessary are, \v 23 and which we think less honorable to be of the body, to these honor greater we put around, and the unpresentable [parts] of us presentability greater have, \v 24 the but presentable [parts] of us not need have.
pieces: Quite the reverse. The parts of the body that seem weaker are all the more necessary.
The parts we think deserve less honor are the very ones we clothe with greater honor, and the parts we do not show are covered with greater care for decency,
while the parts we can show need no such care.

L.22: On the contrary, much more the members of the body that seem to be weaker are necessary,
L.23: and [the parts] of the body that we think to be less honorable, on these we put greater honor, and our [parts] not fit to be seen have greater dignity,
L.24: but our [parts] fit to be seen have no need [of it].

R.22: In fact, the parts of the body that seem weaker are the ones we need even more.
R.23: The parts we think are less important are the ones we honor most. We take extra care to cover the private parts of our body,
R.24: but the parts that others see do not need this care.

decisions.choice: on the contrary, all the more: far from being unneeded, the weaker parts are needed most
decisions.reason: ἀλλὰ answers the eye and head of verse 21, and πολλῷ μᾶλλον strengthens the point.

decisions.choice: seem to be weaker: parts that look frail or unimportant
decisions.reason: δοκοῦντα stresses appearance: they only seem weaker. Paul does not say which parts he means; the soft inner organs or the eyes, which cannot defend themselves, are possible.

decisions.choice: less honorable and unpresentable parts: the parts of the body people keep covered, above all the sexual organs
decisions.reason: περιτίθεμεν means to put something around, as clothing is put on. People honor the parts they think least of by clothing them with care, while the face and hands go uncovered. Paul speaks of this modestly and so does the translation.

decisions.choice: unpresentable, presentability, presentable: a play on words about what is fit to be seen
decisions.reason: ἀσχήμονα and εὐσχήμονα are opposites, and εὐσχημοσύνην is the noun from the same root: decency, propriety. The point is that the parts thought shameful receive more care.

decisions.choice: the picture applies to members of the church whose gifts seem less important
decisions.reason: Paul is preparing to say that God gives more honor to those who lack it (verse 24). The members of the church who seem weakest are needed, and deserve honor.

decisions.choice: [parts] not fit to be seen / fit to be seen (L); the parts we do not show / can show (B); the private parts of our body / the parts that others see (R)
decisions.reason: Each level keeps the contrast between what is covered and what is shown (m4) in plain and modest words (m3).

records.source: ἀλλὰ ὁ θεὸς συνεκέρασεν τὸ σῶμα, τῷ ὑστεροῦντι περισσοτέραν δοὺς τιμήν, ἵνα μὴ ᾖ σχίσμα ἐν τῷ σώματι, ἀλλὰ τὸ αὐτὸ ὑπὲρ ἀλλήλων μεριμνῶσι τὰ μέλη.
records.gloss: But the God blended together the body, to the [part] lacking greater having given honor, \v 25 so that not there be division in the body, but the same for one another may care the members.
pieces: But God has blended the body together and given more honor to the part that falls short,
so that the body would not be split apart, but its parts would all care for one another alike.

L.24: But God mixed the body together, having given more honor to the [part] lacking [it],
L.25: so that there may not be a split in the body, but the members may care the same for one another.

R.24: God put the body together in a way that gives more honor to the parts that need it.
R.25: He did this so that the body would not be divided, and all its parts would care about each other equally.

decisions.choice: blended together: combined the parts into a single well-balanced whole
decisions.reason: συνεκέρασεν is used of mixing things together, such as wine and water. God made one body out of different parts, each in the right measure.

decisions.choice: division: the same word as for the divisions in the church at Corinth
decisions.reason: σχίσμα is the word Paul used for the splits in the church (1:10; 11:18). The body God made has no such splits; neither should the church.

decisions.choice: the same care for one another: equal concern, each part for the others
decisions.reason: τὸ αὐτὸ means "the same": the parts care for one another alike, without favoring some.

decisions.choice: He did this so that
decisions.reason: Readable begins a new sentence for the purpose and names God as the one who acts.

records.source: καὶ εἴτε πάσχει ἓν μέλος, συμπάσχει πάντα τὰ μέλη· εἴτε δοξάζεται μέλος, συγχαίρει πάντα τὰ μέλη.
records.gloss: And whether suffers one member, suffer with [it] all the members; whether is glorified a member, rejoice with [it] all the members.
pieces: If one part is in pain, all the parts share its pain; if one part is honored, all the parts share its joy.

L.26: And if one member suffers, all the members suffer with [it]; if a member is honored, all the members rejoice with [it].

R.26: If one part of the body hurts, all the other parts hurt with it. If one part is honored, all the other parts are glad with it.

decisions.choice: is glorified: is honored, given honor by others
decisions.reason: δοξάζεται usually means to give glory, and often of God. Here it is used of the honor one part of the body receives, as verses 23-24 speak of honor.

decisions.choice: suffer with, rejoice with: the parts share each other's experience
decisions.reason: Both verbs are compounds with "with": the parts suffer together and rejoice together, as Romans 12:15 tells believers to do.

decisions.choice: honored
decisions.reason: The settled word for this verb is "glorify", but here it means human honor, not glory (m1); every level says "honored".

records.source: Ὑμεῖς δέ ἐστε σῶμα Χριστοῦ καὶ μέλη ἐκ μέρους.
records.gloss: You now are body of Christ and members from part.
pieces: You are {{christos:Christ's|the Messiah's}} body, and each of you individually is one of its parts.

L.27: Now you are [the] body of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, and members, each for [your] part.

R.27: Together you are {{christos:Christ's|the Messiah's}} body, and every one of you is a part of that body.

decisions.choice: Christ's body: what the church is, not one body among others
decisions.reason: σῶμα has no article. The phrase says what kind of thing the church is: Christ's body. The church in Corinth is that body where it meets.

decisions.choice: each for your part: individually, each with your own place
decisions.reason: ἐκ μέρους means "in part", "individually": together they are the body, and each is one part of it.

decisions.choice: you are Christ's body: Paul now applies the picture to the Corinthians
decisions.reason: Ὑμεῖς comes first for emphasis. What verses 12-26 said of a body is true of them.

decisions.choice: parts (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 12.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ's|the Messiah's}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

records.heading: You are the body of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}

records.source: καὶ οὓς μὲν ἔθετο ὁ θεὸς ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ πρῶτον ἀποστόλους, δεύτερον προφήτας, τρίτον διδασκάλους, ἔπειτα δυνάμεις, ἔπειτα χαρίσματα ἰαμάτων, ἀντιλήμψεις, κυβερνήσεις, γένη γλωσσῶν.
records.gloss: And whom on the one hand placed the God in the church first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then powers, then gifts of healings, helps, guidings, kinds of tongues.
pieces: In the church God has placed some people: first apostles, second prophets, third teachers. After them come miracles, then gifts of healing, the ability to help, the ability to guide, and different kinds of tongues.

L.28: And those whom God placed in the church [are] first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then miracles, then gifts of healings, helps, guidings, kinds of tongues.

R.28: God has given the church different people for different work. First there are apostles, second prophets, and third teachers. Then there are people who do miracles, people who have gifts to heal, people who help others, people who lead, and people who speak in different kinds of tongues.

decisions.choice: those whom God placed: the sentence starts with people and moves on to gifts
decisions.reason: οὓς μὲν leads us to expect "some ... others", but Paul lists three kinds of people and then changes to gifts. The people and the gifts are both what God has given the church.

decisions.choice: first, second, third: an order of priority for building up the church
alternatives: an order of rank or honor
decisions.reason: Apostles, prophets and teachers are the ones whose speaking lays the church's foundation and builds it up (3:10; 14:1-5; Ephesians 2:20; 4:11). Paul has just said that God gives more honor to the parts that seem lesser (verse 24), so the order is about usefulness, not status. Whether "then" continues the ranking is less clear; tongues come last, as in verse 10.

decisions.choice: apostles: those sent by the risen Christ as his authorized messengers
decisions.reason: Paul counts himself among the apostles (9:1; 15:9) and speaks of more apostles than the Twelve (15:5-7).

decisions.choice: helps: acts of help, especially for the weak and needy
decisions.reason: ἀντιλήμψεις occurs only here in the New Testament. The related verb is used for helping the weak (Acts 20:35).

decisions.choice: guidings: the gift of giving direction and leading the church wisely
decisions.reason: κυβερνήσεις is related to the word for a ship's pilot, the one who steers. In the Greek Old Testament it is the wise counsel by which one is guided (Proverbs 1:5; 11:14). The exact form of leadership is not described.

decisions.choice: helps, guidings (L); the ability to help, the ability to guide (B); people who help others, people who lead (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the bare nouns; Balanced shows that they are gifts, like the others in the list (m4, m5).

decisions.choice: people who do miracles ... people who speak in different kinds of tongues
alternatives: then miracles, then gifts of healing ...
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the whole list in terms of people, so that it reads smoothly; the gifts are named by what the people do (m1).

records.source: μὴ πάντες ἀπόστολοι;
records.gloss: Not all apostles?
pieces: Is everyone an apostle?

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer no
decisions.reason: μὴ marks a question that expects "no". All seven questions in verses 29-30 do the same: not every believer has every gift.

decisions.choice: statements instead of questions (verses 29-30)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the answer each question expects (m1).

records.source: μὴ πάντες προφῆται;
records.gloss: Not all prophets?
pieces: Is everyone a prophet?

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer no
decisions.reason: As in the question before.

records.source: μὴ πάντες διδάσκαλοι;
records.gloss: Not all teachers?
pieces: Is everyone a teacher?

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer no
decisions.reason: As in verse 29a.

records.source: μὴ πάντες δυνάμεις;
records.gloss: Not all powers?
pieces: Does everyone work miracles?

L.29: Not all [are workers of] miracles, [are they]?

decisions.choice: miracles: people who do miracles
decisions.reason: δυνάμεις; is the noun "powers, miracles", as in verse 28; the question means those who do them.

decisions.choice: [workers of] miracles
decisions.reason: Literal supplies what the question means.

records.source: μὴ πάντες χαρίσματα ἔχουσιν ἰαμάτων;
records.gloss: Not all gifts have of healings?
pieces: Does everyone have gifts of healing?

L.30: Not all have gifts of healings, [do they]?

R.30: Not everyone has gifts to heal people.

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer no
decisions.reason: As in verse 29. The gifts are those of verses 9 and 28.

records.source: μὴ πάντες γλώσσαις λαλοῦσιν;
records.gloss: Not all in tongues speak?
pieces: Does everyone speak in tongues?

L.30: Not all speak in tongues, [do they]?

decisions.choice: tongues: the gift of verses 10 and 28
decisions.reason: Speaking in tongues was valued highly in Corinth (14:1-25). Paul says plainly that it is not given to everyone, and so cannot be the sign that someone has the Spirit.

records.source: μὴ πάντες διερμηνεύουσιν;
records.gloss: Not all interpret?
pieces: Does everyone interpret?

R.30: Not everyone can interpret what is said in tongues.

decisions.choice: interpret: put what is said in a tongue into words others understand
decisions.reason: διερμηνεύουσιν; is the verb used for interpreting tongues in 14:5, 13 and 27.

decisions.choice: what is said in tongues
decisions.reason: Readable says what is interpreted (m1).

records.source: ζηλοῦτε δὲ τὰ χαρίσματα τὰ μείζονα.
records.gloss: Be zealous but [for] the gifts the greater.
pieces: But set your hearts on the greater gifts.

L.31: But be zealous for the greater gifts.

R.31: Try hard to receive the greater gifts.

decisions.choice: be zealous: a command
alternatives: you are zealous: a statement, perhaps ironic, about the gifts the Corinthians thought greater
decisions.reason: ζηλοῦτε has the same form for the command and the statement. In 14:1 and 14:39 Paul uses the same verb clearly as a command, for prophecy, a gift he calls greater (14:5). The statement reading takes the verse as describing the Corinthians' rivalry, which chapter 13 then corrects.

decisions.choice: the greater gifts: those that do more to build up the church
alternatives: gifts that give their owner more status
decisions.reason: Chapter 14 explains "greater": prophecy is greater than tongues because it builds up the church (14:5). The greater gifts are the most useful, not the most impressive.

decisions.choice: be zealous for: seek eagerly, set your heart on
decisions.reason: ζηλοῦτε is to be eager for something, to strive for it (14:1, 12). It can be used for jealous rivalry (3:3), but here it is a good eagerness.

decisions.choice: set your hearts on (B); try hard to receive (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what eagerness for a gift means; the footnote gives the statement reading (m1).

records.source: καὶ ἔτι καθ’ ὑπερβολὴν ὁδὸν ὑμῖν δείκνυμι.
records.gloss: And yet according to surpassing a way to you I show.
pieces: And now I will show you a way that is beyond comparison.

L.31: And yet I show you a way beyond all measure.

R.31: But now I will show you a way that is better than anything else.

decisions.choice: and yet, and still: Paul goes on to something more
decisions.reason: ἔτι may go with "beyond all measure" ("a still better way") or with "I show" ("and further, I show you"). The sense is close: what follows goes beyond the seeking of gifts.

decisions.choice: a way beyond all measure: a way better than all others
alternatives: a better way of seeking the gifts
decisions.reason: The phrase "according to surpassing" describes the way: it is better beyond comparison. It is not another gift but a way of life in which all the gifts are used.

decisions.choice: the way is love, which chapter 13 describes
decisions.reason: Paul often speaks of a way of life (4:17). Chapter 13 shows that without love every gift is worthless, and 14:1 joins the two: pursue love, and be eager for the gifts.

decisions.choice: I show: Paul is about to show them
decisions.reason: The present δείκνυμι looks to what Paul is about to write.

decisions.choice: I will show you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say that the showing comes next (m4).
